name: Healthy Shepherd's Pie
desc: Ground beef, vegetables, and cabbage in a tomato sauce, baked under a mashed parsnip topping instead of potatoes.

source.title: Healthy Shepherd's Pie
source.evidence: Same beef, onion, garlic, carrot, celery, diced tomato, tomato paste, chicken stock and green cabbage filling under a parsnip puree loosened with stock, at the same 375°F; this version skips the cornstarch, garlic powder and Worcestershire.

ingredients.raw: 2 large or 4 small carrots, finely diced
1 small head green cabbage, thinly sliced (about 4 cups)
8 to 10 parsnips (about 2 1/4 lb), peeled and cut into 1-inch slices

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil for the parsnips.

Filling: heat the olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat. Add the onion, garlic, carrots, celery, and beef and cook, breaking up the meat, until the beef is browned with no pink left and the vegetables are soft, 8-10 min.
Drain off the fat if there is a lot. Add the drained tomatoes, tomato paste, 1 cup chicken stock, 2 tsp salt, and 1 tsp pepper, and stir until the paste is blended in.

Add the cabbage, bring to a simmer, and reduce to medium-low. Cook until the sauce thickens and the cabbage is tender, about 10 min. Transfer to a 5-quart baking dish (or a 9x13 in dish at least 2 inches deep) and spread level.
Parsnips: while the filling simmers, add the parsnips to the boiling water and cook until very tender when pierced with a knife, 10-15 min. Drain well.
Mash the parsnips with the 1 1/2 cups chicken stock, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tsp pepper until smooth (a food processor gives the smoothest result).
Spread the parsnip mash over the filling. Bake until the filling bubbles at the edges and the top is lightly browned, about 20 min.
Rest 5 min, then scatter with the parsley and chives and serve.
tips: The Modern Proper version bakes 30 to 35 min for more browning on top and thickens the filling with 2 tbsp cornstarch whisked into the stock; add the cornstarch if your filling looks loose.
